answer_first: We print a replacement center console lid latch designed to fit the Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra 2007-2013 bucket-seat console, in PETG. Send a photo of the old latch and your year, and we quote within 24 hours on business days, from $19.

problem: The console latch breaks and the lid will not stay shut, so it flaps open over bumps and corners. It is a small part, but the console is used every drive. People often cannot tell whether the latch or the lid itself has failed.
oem_situation: A cheap fix exists: one retailer lists an aftermarket 2-pack of latches (GM 20864151/53/54) for $8.99, and a single latch for $25.95. If the cheap latch fits your truck, buy it. A made-to-fit printed part makes sense when your year or color does not match, the part is discontinued, or the latch keeps breaking and you want a different material.
our_part: We print PETG, which holds up in a warm cabin where PLA softens, and we can use ASA if the vehicle sits in strong sun. We do not use PLA for car interiors. We need a photo of the old latch or the empty position, with a coin or ruler in the shot, and your year and model. Interior trim only; we do not make airbag, seatbelt, brake, steering, lighting or fuel parts.

how_to_order: Photograph the broken latch, or the empty latch position on the console, with a coin in the shot. Note your year and model.
Send photos on the request page, with any part number you can see. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

faqs.q: Why not just buy the $8.99 aftermarket pair?
faqs.a: If it fits your truck and you are happy with it, do that. Ours is for when the year or color does not match, the part is discontinued, or the latch keeps breaking and you want a different material.

faqs.q: Is a printed latch as strong as the original?
faqs.a: We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. We tell you if the part is a poor candidate.

faqs.q: Will it handle heat in a parked truck?
faqs.a: PLA softens in a hot car, so we do not use it. We print PETG for cabins and can use ASA if the vehicle sits in strong sun.

faqs.q: How do I photograph the latch for a fit check?
faqs.a: Photograph the latch and its mating spot on the lid from the front, side and underside, on a plain background with a coin or ruler. Send your year, model and any part number on the old piece. The photo also tells us whether the latch or the lid is the part that failed.

faqs.q: Do you make safety-related car parts?
faqs.a: No. We make interior and trim parts only, and we do not make airbag, seatbelt, brake, steering, lighting or fuel parts.
